title: A Player Collapsed After Match Point. The World Number Two Was Eliminated. Djokovic Saved a Match Point at Thirty-Nine. This Was Day Four at Roland Garros.
excerpt: Jakub Mensik was wheeled off court after a five-set war in 32°C heat. Elena Rybakina committed 71 unforced errors and lost to world number 55. Novak Djokovic survived a third-set scare. The 2026 French Open keeps delivering.
body:
Wednesday at Roland Garros was supposed to be a transitional day. Second-round matches. Routine progression for the favourites. Instead, it produced a medical emergency, the tournament's biggest upset, and a 39-year-old fighting through sweltering heat to stay alive in the draw.

## Mensik Collapses on Court 6

The most frightening image of the day came from Court 6, where 20-year-old Czech Jakub Mensik collapsed to the ground moments after winning match point against Argentina's Mariano Navone.

Mensik had just survived a near-five-hour war — 6-3, 2-6, 6-4, 1-6, 7-6(11) — with the deciding tiebreak going to 13 points. He won the match. Then his body gave out.

Medical staff rushed onto court. Mensik was treated with ice packs for severe leg cramps. He was eventually helped up, walked a few steps, and collapsed again. He was taken off in a wheelchair.

"The heat was insane," Mensik said afterwards. "You have no time to cool down between games. You sit on the changeover for ninety seconds and you're right back in 32 degrees on the clay."

The incident is the most dramatic in a tournament that has been plagued by extreme conditions. Four players had already retired or withdrawn due to heat-related issues before Wednesday. Casper Ruud reported cramping. Multiple players have called for schedule adjustments during the hottest afternoon hours.

Boris Becker, watching from the commentary booth, called the conditions "borderline." Medical experts cited heat cramps and dehydration as the primary risks. The broader question is whether Grand Slams — with their best-of-five-set format for men — need to fundamentally reconsider scheduling in an era of increasingly extreme weather.

The French Open has a heat rule that allows 10-minute breaks when temperatures exceed certain thresholds, but it was not activated on Wednesday despite conditions reaching 32°C on the exposed clay courts. Novak Djokovic, who played his own gruelling match the same day, urged organizers to consider rescheduling matches during peak afternoon hours.

## Rybakina's Shocking Exit

On Court Suzanne-Lenglen, the biggest upset of the tournament unfolded in slow motion.

Elena Rybakina, the world number two and a two-time Grand Slam champion, was eliminated by Yuliia Starodubtseva, ranked 55th in the world. The score: 3-6, 6-1, 7-6(10-4).

Rybakina won the first set comfortably. Then she fell apart. She committed 71 unforced errors across the match — a staggering number for a player of her calibre. Her serve, usually one of the most devastating weapons in women's tennis, misfired repeatedly. The heat appeared to affect her movement and decision-making as the match wore on.

Starodubtseva, 26, is no stranger to French Open upsets. In 2024, she defeated Jasmine Paolini at Roland Garros. But beating the world number two — a former Wimbledon champion and back-to-back Australian Open winner — is a different order of magnitude entirely.

The loss leaves the women's draw without one of its genuine title contenders. With both Rybakina and Sabalenka's path now clearer, Iga Swiatek — the four-time champion — advanced comfortably on the same day, beating Sara Bejlek 6-2, 6-3. She moves into the third round as the overwhelming favourite.

The ranking implications are significant. Rybakina's early exit means Aryna Sabalenka, the world number one, now has a 587-point cushion. A deep run by Sabalenka could push her ranking points past 10,000 — a threshold last achieved by Ashleigh Barty.

## Djokovic at 39: Still Here

On the main court, Philippe Chatrier, Novak Djokovic reminded everyone that age is a number he has never particularly respected.

The three-time French Open champion, now 39, defeated Frenchman Valentin Royer 6-3, 6-2, 6-7(7), 6-3 in three hours and 28 minutes. He saved a match point in the third-set tiebreak — a moment that would have ended anyone else's tournament — and then closed out the fourth set in clinical fashion.

Djokovic became only the fourth man in the professional era to reach the third round in Paris after his 39th birthday. He has now won 30 consecutive matches against French players at Roland Garros, a streak stretching back more than two decades. It is his 21st third-round appearance at the French Open, tying the all-time record.

"It was really important for me to close it out in four," Djokovic said. "In these conditions, you don't want to go to a fifth."

He next faces 18-year-old Brazilian Joao Fonseca, seeded 28th. The generational gap is extraordinary — Djokovic is more than twice Fonseca's age. The young Brazilian is one of the most exciting talents in tennis, having beaten Jack Draper and Tommy Paul this season. But clay remains Djokovic's kingdom.

## More Seeds Fall

Elsewhere, Alexander Bublik, the ninth seed, was eliminated by Jan-Lennard Struff in four sets. Haddad Maia, the 25th-ranked Brazilian, fell to Francesca Jones in three. The draw continues to thin at an alarming rate.

Belinda Bencic, the 2021 Olympic champion returning after a two-year absence from the French Open, powered past Caty McNally 6-4, 6-0 to become the first woman into the third round. Mirra Andreeva, the eighth seed, also advanced comfortably.

## India's Day at Roland Garros

For Indian tennis, the day was quiet. Nishesh Basavareddy's singles run ended in the second round on Tuesday with a straight-sets loss to Michael Michelsen. But Yuki Bhambri and Sriram Balaji remain alive in the men's doubles draw, having won their second-round match on Day 3.

They are India's last two representatives at the 2026 French Open. Both are experienced doubles campaigners, and their partnership has been productive on the European clay season. A deep doubles run would be the best Indian result at Roland Garros in years.

## What Comes Next

Thursday brings the completion of the second round and the start of the third round. The heat is expected to persist through the week. And the tournament is only halfway through its opening phase.

For viewers in India, Roland Garros coverage is available on Sony Sports Network and SonyLIV. The matches begin at 2:30 PM IST, with the marquee court sessions starting at 4:30 PM IST.

The 2026 French Open has delivered more drama in four days than most Grand Slams produce in a fortnight. And the second week hasn't even begun.
